title: Resistivity
examples: What does the symbol rho represent in the resistance formula?
If I use a thicker wire, what happens to its resistance?
Does the material of the wire change how much it resists electricity?

explain.say: Today we are learning about resistivity in electrical circuits.
Resistivity is a property of the material itself.
Resistance is calculated using the formula R equals rho times L divided by A.
The resistance R depends on the resistivity rho, the length L, and the cross-sectional area A.
A longer wire of the same material has a higher resistance.
In real life, the length of a heating element affects its resistance. A longer element will heat up more.

faq.q: What is the difference between resistance and resistivity?
faq.a: Resistance is a measured value for a specific object. Resistivity is an intrinsic property of the material itself.
asks: Is resistivity the same as resistance?

faq.q: Does the material always determine the resistance?
faq.a: No, the shape and size also matter. The formula shows length and area are important factors too.
asks: Does the wire's shape matter for resistance?
Only the material matters for resistance?

faq.q: If I use a bigger wire, does the resistance go up or down?
faq.a: If you use a bigger wire, meaning a larger cross-sectional area, the resistance will go down.
asks: Does bigger area mean more resistance?

faq.q: What are the standard units for resistivity?
faq.a: The standard unit for resistivity is the ohm meter, written as the Greek letter omega.
asks: What unit is used for resistivity?
What is the unit symbol for resistivity?

faq.a: Yes, temperature changes can change the resistivity of most materials. This is a key factor to remember.

facts: Resistivity ($\rho$) is a characteristic property of the material.
Resistance (R) depends on material, length, and area.
The formula relating them is R equals $\rho$ times L divided by A.
Copper has a low resistivity, making it a good conductor.

quiz.say: If you cut a wire in half, what happens to its resistance?
quiz.why: Cutting the wire halves the length, and resistance is directly proportional to length.

wrong.1: This incorrectly relates halving the length to squaring the change.
wrong.2: This ignores the direct relationship between length and resistance.
wrong.3: This uses an incorrect mathematical relationship.

quiz.say: A wire has a resistance of six ohms. If you use a wire with twice the area, what is the new resistance?
quiz.why: Resistance is inversely proportional to area. Doubling the area halves the resistance.

wrong.1: This incorrectly multiplies the resistance by the change in area.
wrong.2: This assumes area has no effect on resistance.
wrong.3: This assumes the relationship is cubic instead of inverse.
